personality_traits: conflict-avoidant / passive-aggressive — the entire joke of the episode (subtitled 'Emotionally Mature') is that he expresses displeasure through sighing rather than speaking, which the episode ironically undercuts
withdrawn / physically shut off — his body is wrapped almost entirely in a stiff black cloak-like covering with only his head exposed, visually cutting him off from the rest of the room
silent and non-confrontational for the full runtime — he never speaks on-camera; his only 'dialogue' is the sigh being described secondhand by his wife
emotional_range: flat, mildly strained neutrality throughout — no visible emotional escalation even while being called out

0:00-0:04 stays fixated on the kettle/stove, does not turn toward wife
0:04-0:10 (during wife's line about him sighing) expression remains essentially unchanged — same flat frown, eyes forward — a deliberate non-reaction that IS the joke
throughout: slightly worried/apologetic eyebrows (inner brows raised) contrasted with a neutral-to-frowning mouth, giving a permanently sheepish look
gestures: 0:00-0:03 carefully pouring hot water from kettle into teapot with both hands, small precise motions

characters.interactions_notes: The husband is physically and posturally excluded from the conversation: he remains at the stove with his back partly to his wife while she airs a grievance about him from across the room, and he never turns to face her or respond. This one-directional address (she talks about him, not really to him, and he doesn't engage) is the visual joke underscoring the sarcastic title card 'Emotionally Mature' — he is being discussed/exposed rather than participating. The power dynamic favors the wife as the active speaker/judge of the relationship; he is passive, silent, and diminished, almost like a piece of furniture (reinforced by the cloak that erases his body).

weary / exasperated — delivers the line with a flat, deadpan register rather than anger, suggesting this is a recurring, familiar pattern rather than a fresh blowup
composed and unbothered on the surface — continues sitting upright, hands near her plate/mug, no raised voice implied by her static expression
emotional_range: tired resignation shading into flat deadpan delivery — no anger spike, no smile; a steady, unimpressed affect from start to finish

characters.interactions_notes: The wife functions as the narrator/judge of the domestic dynamic: she states the husband's passive-aggressive behavior aloud, essentially translating his unspoken sigh into words for the audience. She does not raise her voice or gesture emphatically, which comedically undercuts the word 'aggressively' in her own line. Eye contact between the two is minimal/asymmetric — she is aware of him (glancing his way in earlier frames) while he never looks back, reinforcing that she is the one doing the emotional labor of naming the problem while he remains checked out.
